title: Updating the Volunteer Handbook
text:
The Riverside Community Center is revising its volunteer handbook before a new group begins work next month. The old handbook was written quickly and contains several expressions that are common in casual speech but are not appropriate for a formal workplace guide. The coordinator wants the new version to sound clear and professional without becoming stiff or difficult to read.

One section explains where volunteers should leave personal items, how they should report schedule changes, and whom they should contact if they cannot attend a shift. Another section describes the effect of late arrivals on the front desk, where only two people may be available during busy periods. The coordinator also wants to distinguish between rules that apply to all volunteers and suggestions that simply make the work easier.

During editing, the team agrees to avoid unnecessary slang and to choose words according to their exact grammatical job. They also check commonly confused words instead of relying only on how a sentence sounds. The goal is not to make every sentence formal for its own sake. The goal is to use standard English that is precise, respectful, and easy for volunteers to follow.
